text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card (14.4% of 571, expected 2.7%, risk score 6.40, z 1.71, 28% low complexity, 0 documented claims). The summary is cautious and correctly flags that no documentation came back. However, the 'inconclusive' call and headline undersell strong claim-level evidence: a 5.36x ratio to expected and about 67 excess 99215 claims. The by_complexity table shows 99215 share exceeding the all-provider share in every complexity band. The summary omits all of this, so an investigator would have to redo the analysis. The two example claims are the first two rows of the low-complexity list, and they cite patients with a single chronic condition, which is weak. Cleaner examples were available (R21, J06.9 claims with 0 conditions). The next steps are generic. Requesting records 'for a larger sample' doesn't name the cited claims or provider-level cases, and it doesn't say that none of the 571 claims had documentation reviewed. The headline 'too few returned records' is vague.","problems":["Omits the ratio to expected (5.36x) and the excess 99215 claims (~66.7), the strongest quantitative points","Does not use the by-complexity breakdown to show 99215 over-use at every complexity level","Example claims are weak (single chronic condition, diabetes and COPD) when 0-condition 99215 claims such as C0049384 (J06.9) were available","Next steps are generic; they don't name specific claim IDs to request documentation for","The headline does not state the finding (elevated 99215 rate vs expected) and only mentions missing records","The 'inconclusive' leaning ignores that 72% of 99215 claims were not low complexity and that the high-complexity claims were not discussed"]}
